title: Montréal shoebox house
form: Compact one-storey house with a rectangular plan and flat roof
description: A shoebox is a small, one-storey home with a flat roof. Montréal examples sit within neighbourhoods that also contain duplexes and triplexes. This original teaching design uses a modest brick front, central entrance and shallow cornice. It illustrates an urban house form, not a particular historic property.
lookFor: One storey under a flat roof
A central door between two windows
Modest brick frontage and shallow cornice
planningConnections: Comparing small homes with taller plexes
designQuestion: How could this small home adapt while keeping its contribution to the street?
componentLimit: A single house does not establish neighbourhood density, ownership, current affordability or a planning ideology.
evidenceBasis: City of Montréal typology/history context plus original generated reference pixels; exact metric scale, unseen structure and internal plan are architectural inferences.
